properties.description:
Required MVP capability: inspect the composed data model actually used by a Broccoli view in an ergonomic runtime UI. Required acceptance examples are the relational engine's OWN composed data model and the Activity board's Task, Input, Evidence and related types.

Required outcomes
1. Expose the actual active model composition, its types, fields, relations and contributor ownership. Distinguish type definitions from the object instances conforming to them; allow navigation to relevant instance data without conflating the two.
2. Inspect predicates, their typed inputs and the bindings that require them to hold. A predicate can consume one field, multiple fields or instances/collections spanning any model types. Do not require separate invariant categories for those cases; expose the actual inputs and dependencies.
3. Selecting a rule identifies its participating types, fields and relations, executable predicate, faithful generated explanation, source/owner and the mutation boundary that enforces it. Inspection of the model and validation results for particular instances must remain distinguishable.
4. The visible model must be derived from the active compiled contributor contracts and their composed rules, never a manually maintained duplicate schema. Show provenance and incomplete/unavailable scope explicitly.
5. Reuse the app's node list, graph and detail/editor views. Provide search and focused relationship scope, a full-height workspace, and directed dependency edges without edge labels in the central data-model graph. Complex models must remain navigable without displaying every instance or relation at once.
6. Evaluate the actual Activity board model at desktop and narrow widths, verify rule-to-field/relation navigation, and independently review the design, plan and implementation.

The attached image is a design proposal with illustrative rules and contributor names, not an approved pixel specification or a claim that the shown UI already exists. In particular its example Task/Input/Evidence context predicate illustrates inter-object invariants; it does not add a new domain rule.
Implementation proposal: https://chatgpt.com/space/page_32d7e631f44c81918b8b209a8cd40398
Source discussion: codex://threads/01a0f501-1ed3-79c1-b149-c5ca4f09243d
The separately deferred generic view request/connection inspector remains outside this task.

Engine self-inspection and corrected UI direction
7. The engine must expose its own Type, Field, Function/predicate, Invariant binding, instance-of association, contributor and composition definitions through the same generated metadata and query path as contributor models. Inspect Type itself as an ordinary type node, including its instance-of relation; no independently authored meta-schema.
8. Type definitions are nodes: selecting one opens the existing node editor. Reuse the editor for its fields, relations and predicate nodes instead of inventing a dedicated type/invariant detail panel. The graph remains useful for navigating their relationships.
9. Corrections to the attached proposal: remove the Activity board / Personal buildspace breadcrumb, the Design proposal badge and the Task neighborhood selector. Replace the custom right-hand Task/Fields/Invariants/Relations inspector with the standard node editor. Keep the central data-model graph with only directed dependency relations and no edge labels. These corrections supersede those parts of the attached image.

The one-file engine model draft is a design exercise. MVP acceptance requires seeing the actual loaded engine model at runtime, not displaying that source file or a hand-built diagram alone.

Dependency-based model browsing
10. The user approved the UI mockup for a first usable implementation. The user will review the relational engine model through that implemented UI, without being required to review TypeScript first, then use the same UI for other models.
11. The left view is named Cluster list and presents clusters of types connected by dependencies rather than a flat list of individual types. Include referenced object types when determining these dependencies, as explicitly confirmed by the user. Shared references may connect contributors into the same cluster; do not invent contributor or topic boundaries to split it.
12. The central graph displays types and only their dependency edges, including dependencies on referenced object types, using horizontal dependency-depth rows: depth 0 at the top, followed by successive depths downward. Dependencies sit above the types that use them; depth must follow dependencies rather than arbitrary visual placement. Display shared types once, retain arrow direction without edge labels, and retain cycles/return edges. The dependency-only and unlabeled-edge requirements apply to this central data-model graph, not to graph UI globally. Individual field definitions and predicate instances are not the nodes of this graph.
13. Use the actual current node editor component and its controls, Fields and Additional relations sections. It provides field details and intra/inter-field invariant inspection; do not redesign it as a bespoke model inspector.
14. The latest image is a UI layout proposal, not authoritative model data; raster-generated edge routing must not define relations. Runtime edges and clusters must come from actual loaded model metadata.

First usable implementation scope
15. Name the center view Dependency graph. Omit its footer/count; use the existing expandable search icon in Cluster list without a permanently visible search input.
16. Start with inspection of current type definitions, their dependencies, and intra-field/inter-field invariants in the existing node editor. Cross-type invariant inspection is deferred from this first version. State extraction and validation coverage accurately; do not portray the proposed transaction/self-model draft as an implemented runtime model.

Context and input boundaries — accepted 2026-10-02
17. Exclude intrinsic JavaScript/TypeScript primitives and compiler utility/library machinery from the dependency graph; semantic type definitions and field type expressions remain inspectable.
18. Available views are discovered through one shared applicability contract from the data supplied to each panel. Buildspace configuration consumes the Buildspace collection and composes Node list plus Node editor. One selected Buildspace supplies a top-level Buildspace composite (Chat plus Work) and Node editor as alternatives on that same node. Work receives activity and repository capabilities; Activity data alone does not imply Data model availability.
19. Reuse the repository tree plus right-hand viewer composition between Review Changes and current Files. Current Files represents the checkouts used by the running instance. Registered system models can be accessed without selecting folders; no selection uses all available models in the current repository/buildspace scope. Selected system folders narrow that scope, while file selection supplies its actual content to applicable text views.
20. Derive model scope from explicit owning-system registrations and checkout provenance. Do not substitute the host catalog for an unrelated buildspace. Missing or stale compiled metadata is visibly unavailable. Cluster membership still follows actual type dependencies; ownership supplies names and scope, not arbitrary cluster partitions.

Usability corrections — accepted 2026-10-02
21. Collapse and restore must reallocate all available pane space without blank reserved columns or overlapping panes. Reproduce nested splitter sequences and correct the shared allocation contract.
22. Present the repository tree as a File tree view. Put current-files versus working-tree scope in a dropdown among its view tools; retain archived review iteration access.
23. Show separators between dependency-depth rows and numeric depth labels fixed against horizontal scrolling. Center node labels. Support Ctrl+wheel zoom and a true Fit without an arbitrary minimum scale.

Existing implementation and remaining acceptance
The current UI already includes the file tree, dependency clusters and graph, and node editor composition described above. Preserve its existing evidence. This task is not a request to build that UI again.

The 2026-10-08 full checkpoint exposed four failing tests covering active-model coverage, exported operation/query contracts, loaded engine definitions and native invariant bindings. Their model catalog results are empty or missing required types. Investigate the actual compiled registration/provenance path and repair it before asking the user to review the model. Do not substitute a hand-authored schema, hide missing types or weaken the expected contract.

Then demonstrate the actual loaded engine and Activity model with typed fields, dependencies, declared invariant coverage and current source provenance through the existing UI. Extend that surface only for missing review needs. Keep cross-type inspection coverage explicit and retain the accepted staged scope above. The next task proposes the execution/review model after this inspection surface passes its named review.
properties.title: Inspect composed data models and their invariants at runtime
